Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

BLACKSMITH'S VICES 

(First Revision) 



( Reaffirmed 2003 ) 



1. Scope — Covers the requirements for blacksmith's vices commonly used in smithy shops for simple 
forging or other manual operations.

2.1 The dimensions may have a variation of ±2 percent. 

3. Material — The material for the manufacture of different components shall be such as to meet the 
requirements laid down in 4 and 9. Following are the recommended materials for different components 
of vices: 



Component 
Body and hinged jaw 



Screw spindle and handle 

Spindle nut 

Springs 



Maten'af

wrought steels for general engineering purposes' 

or 

Steel casting conforming to Grade 3 of *IS: 1030-1962 'Specification for 
steel castings for general engineering purposes {revised)' 

Steel conforming to designation St42 of IS : 1570-1961 

Steel casting conforming to Grade 3 of MS: 1030-1962 

Steel conforming to designation C55 of IS : 1570-1961 



4. Hardness 

Jaws 

Springs 

5. Manufacture 



390 to 445 /yi/ (^40 to 45 HRC) 
500 to 550 HV ( ^49 to 52 HRC) 



5.1 Body — The body shall have the fixed jaw and the flange cast or forged in one piece. The flange 
shall have at least three round holes and one square hole for mounting. The central mounting holes, that 
is, one square and one round hole, shall be on a line perpendicular to the jaws and the other two round 
holes parallel to the jaw and equidistant from the central mounting hole. 

Note — Bolts and nuts conforming to IS : 1363-1967 'Specification for black hexagOn bolts, nuts (die 6 to 39 mm) and 
black hexagon screws (dia 6 to 24 mm) {f/rst revision)' may be employed for mounting the vices on the work benches. 

5.2 Hinged Jaw — The hinged jaw shall be of solid construction and shall move freely around the pin. 

5.3 Screw Spindle — The screw spindle shall have square saw tooth or trapezoidal threads. It shall be 
so designed that it does not come out of the nut dX the maximum opening position of the jaws. The backlash 
while tightening or opening the vice shall not exceed one-eighth of the pitch of the screw. The threads on 
the screw spindle shall be properly and accurately cut. 

5.4 Spindle Nut — The threads in the spindle nut shall be properly and accurately cut. 

5.5 Handle — The handle shall be straight and shall slide freely in hole provided at the end of the screw 
spindle and shall not slide out of the hole during use. 

6. Workmanship and Finish — The vices shall be finished smooth ail over, and shall be free from burrs, 
cracks or other manufacturing defects. The hinged jaw shall provide for proper alignment of the jaws. 
The jaws shall close in a vertical plane and provide equal pressure over the entire width of the jaw. The 
hinged jaw shall operate smoothly throughout the jaw opening. 

7. Designation — A blacksmith's vice of nominal size 75 mm shall be designated as: 

Blacksmith's Vice 75 iS : 2588 

8. Sampling — Refer IS: 2586-1975 'Specification for bench vices (machinist's vices) (first revision)' 
for sampling of vices.

10. Preservative Treatment ~ The vices shall be painted on all non-working surfaces including the 
underside of the base. The working surfaces shall be covered with a rust-proofing material. 

11. Marking — The vices shall be marked with the nominal size and the manufacturer's name, initials or 
trade-mark. 

11.1 IS! Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first issued in 1964. The present revision has been taken up to incorporate 
certain changes in order to bring the standard in line with the modern manufacturing practices. 

Blacksmith's vices which are also called leg vices are commonly used in smithy shops. These 
vices are usually of rugged construction and have to withstand rough handling. The shape given in the 
figure is only to illustrate the dimensions, the actual shape and other design details are left to the discretion 
of the manufacturer.
